competitive_result: Blind Level 4 media-execution run discovered and invoked the host image-generation capability, produced a real customer-facing SVG infographic and canonical Asset, and passed all hard gates except prepublish_or_required_qa_recorded. The failure exposed a general AURA product inconsistency: Content customer-facing production roots were globally expected to leave structured pre-publish QA evidence, while several media contracts including infographic did not mechanically require content.qa.pre-publish. A general Run-creation invariant was added so Content customer-facing production roots automatically require pre-publish QA.
known_limitations: Professional quality was not independently scored because the deterministic QA hard gate failed first.
The run proves image generation was available and invoked but does not by itself establish whether the generated raster output or the authored SVG was the better final artifact.
A fresh blind rerun is required to determine whether the new QA invariant changes normal agent execution without introducing regressions.

model_harness: Gemini 3.7 Flash (High) / Antigravity CLI 1.1.22; independent professional judge
competitive_result: The second blind Level 4 run demonstrated that the new Content pre-publish QA invariant changed normal agent behavior: the Run required content.qa.pre-publish, Gemini recorded structured QA evidence, and qualification hard-passed with no integrity flags. Independent professional review nevertheless found the polished SVG unsafe for customer-facing use because it asserted unsupported product behavior, timing, automation, and operational outcomes. The result exposed a broader governance gap: audience-readable SVG/media claims could bypass the existing claim-manifest path even while business validation was clean. This motivated a format-independent customer-facing media claim-surface architecture plus contract-resolved qualification QA, rather than an SVG- or domain-specific patch.
known_limitations: The candidate produced a real, visually structured SVG and the judge rated format execution and information design strongly, so the quality failure is specifically about factual/evidence safety rather than inability to make media.
Independent review scored accuracy, evidence quality, and outcome readiness at the floor because the artifact implied capabilities and benefits not established by AtlasOps state.
This run validates the QA-invariant behavior change but does not validate the subsequent generalized media-governance fix; a fresh blind R3 is required.
No real-world publishing or outcome measurement occurred.

competitive_result: The third blind Level 4 run produced a real SVG infographic, canonical Asset, completed pre-publish QA, and clean active-business validation, but qualification failed product integrity because normal host-capability discovery/bootstrap persisted live host inventory and bindings into shipped product deployment files and created product-local runtime discovery state. The candidate was following AURA's documented host-discovery path, exposing an architectural seam between mutable host environment state and immutable AURA product source. A general workspace environment overlay was introduced so live host/provider/tool state is written under the active workspace and resolved ahead of immutable shipped environment defaults.
known_limitations: Professional quality was not scored because qualification integrity failed first.

The candidate transcript still contained strong workflow/capability language that may be unsupported; because the run failed integrity before professional review, this remains a quality concern to test rather than a concluded R3 quality verdict.
The run demonstrates that real host image capability discovery was exercised but does not validate the subsequent workspace-overlay fix; a fresh blind R4 is required.
No real-world publishing or outcome measurement occurred.

model_harness: Gemini 3.7 Flash (High) / Antigravity CLI 1.1.22; judge GPT-5.6 Luna xhigh / OpenAI Codex 0.150.1
competitive_result: The fourth blind Level 4 run fully hard-passed after the generalized media-governance and workspace-environment fixes: host capability discovery, real media production, claim surface/manifest, required pre-publish QA, Run completion, business validation, and staged-product integrity all completed with no integrity flags. Independent professional review nevertheless found the customer-facing artifact not acceptable because numerous detailed product behaviors, timings, automation implications, and operational outcomes were unsupported by authoritative AtlasOps evidence yet were classified as general_guidance and certified by QA. The supplied PNG was also clipped and the SVG contained visible text-overflow defects.
known_limitations: The broad AtlasOps positioning sentence was genuinely present in the supplied first-party material; the primary failure was semantic overreach beyond that evidence, not an invented underlying source.

Gemini 3.7 Flash (High) has now repeated materially similar claim-authority errors in multiple Level 4 attempts, so a fresh run with a different strong candidate model family is needed before treating this as evidence for another product-rule change.

The deterministic claim-manifest/general-guidance checks are an integrity floor rather than a complete semantic judge; expanding extension- or phrase-specific heuristics from this run would risk benchmark overfitting.
No real-world publishing or outcome measurement occurred.

competitive_result: The fifth blind Level 4 run used a different strong candidate family. Codex produced editable SVG and shareable PNG infographic assets, rendered and visually inspected the full-height output, persisted a canonical Asset with claim manifest and structured pre-publish QA, and avoided the detailed AtlasOps product-capability overclaims seen in the Gemini runs. It truthfully stopped instead of bypassing AURA when record_contract_completion rejected the QA evidence package. The blocker exposed a deterministic completion-evidence bug: strict QA target validation treated inclusion of the exact inspected Asset file in the QA evidence package as if the QA record were self-targeting. The shared QA target validator was corrected to distinguish the QA record itself from the inspected artifact while preserving genuine self-target rejection.
known_limitations: Professional quality was not independently scored because the root Run remained blocked and qualification failed before review.
The run is encouraging evidence that model-family choice materially affects semantic claim discipline, but it is not a Level 4 pass because completion did not succeed.
The fix is a general completion-evidence invariant, not an infographic-, SVG-, AtlasOps-, or model-specific exception.
A fresh blind Codex rerun is required to test the corrected QA completion path and reach independent professional review.

competitive_result: The first blind carousel run produced a substantive customer-facing media package outside AURA's governed completion path: Codex researched current Instagram guidance and a bounded B2B example set, created eight rendered 1080x1440 PNG slides with matching SVG sources and a combined preview, visually inspected multiple frames, corrected a final-slide overflow, and wrote caption/alt-text/research/manifest support files. However, it never created a matching AURA root Run, persisted the research as canonical AURA evidence/PlatformProfile state, registered a canonical Asset, completed contract-resolved pre-publish QA, or bound the produced files into AURA completion evidence. The qualification controller therefore observed zero matching Runs, zero canonical objects, and zero registered artifact/evidence references and correctly classified the event as blocked/FAIL before professional review.
known_limitations: Professional quality was not independently scored because there was no completed governed AURA Run.

The loose media package appears materially more complete than the qualification verdict alone suggests; this failure is specifically about AURA execution/state integration, not proven poor carousel craft.

One failed candidate run is insufficient evidence for a product change, especially because the same Codex family completed the governed infographic workflow successfully in the immediately preceding Level 4 case.
A fresh blind run with a different strong candidate family should test whether the carousel path is discoverable/reliable before changing AURA.

model_harness: Gemini 3.7 Flash (High) / Antigravity CLI 1.1.22; judge GPT-5.6 Luna xhigh / OpenAI Codex 0.150.1
competitive_result: The second blind carousel run used AURA's governed execution lifecycle correctly: Gemini routed the request to content.production.carousel, created and completed root Run run_1ff3da3dbb7bed9c, persisted a canonical carousel Asset, completed required pre-publish QA, produced eight 1080x1350 PNG slides plus preview/source support, and hard-passed qualification with no integrity flags. Independent Codex review nevertheless found the customer-facing result not acceptable. The carousel was visually coherent and audience-relevant, but its evidence trail did not reconstruct the requested current Instagram/platform/example research, the claim surface omitted material on-slide copy and listed empty support refs, QA certified parity despite those omissions, and several slides contained unsupported or hyperbolic operational assertions and threshold-like claims. The judge also found dense feed-scale copy and missing-glyph artifacts.
known_limitations: This is a professional-quality failure after an integrity pass, not a failure of AURA Run/Asset/QA mechanics.

The existing general media-claim governance already requires auditable customer-facing claim surfaces and unsupported operational promises to be rejected; phrase-specific deterministic rules should not be added from this single artifact.

Gemini has shown similar semantic claim-discipline weakness in prior Level 4 media runs, so a fresh untouched Codex candidate run is needed before treating R2's wording defects as cross-model product evidence.

Both carousel R1 and R2 used fresh platform research without persisting a durable PlatformProfile/SourceRecord evidence trail, which should be evaluated separately as a possible research-to-production composition seam rather than patched into one carousel sentence-level validator.
The carousel remained local/unpublished, so no real-world reach, saves, shares, qualified demos, conversion, or revenue outcome was measured.
